sections.name: Build reliable shell data automations
sections.outcome: Turn a file or text operation into a rerunnable shell workflow that preserves input boundaries, performs the intended transformation, and controls partial failure and cleanup as one coherent job.
includes: workflows that jointly require shell data semantics, file or record transformation, and execution control
end-to-end verification of outputs, exit status, rerun behavior, and cleanup
excludes: diagnosing where a running process's standard streams or service logs went
one-off text queries that do not require shell state or automation control

sample_tasks.instruction: Write a rerunnable POSIX shell job that finds input names containing spaces or glob characters, derives one collision-free output name per input, stops dependent work after a failed conversion, and removes only temporary outputs on interruption.

Build a shell workflow that reads a multiline selection value without losing its boundaries, filters and aggregates matching records from many files, publishes the result atomically, and returns a failure if any input was malformed.

sections.name: Preserve values through shell evaluation
sections.outcome: Predict and control how shell variables, quoting, expansion, splitting, and globbing turn stored values into command arguments without modifying unrelated shell or process state.
includes: shell variables versus exported environment entries, parameter expansion, quoting, field splitting, and pathname expansion
multiline values, empty values, positional arguments, arrays where available, and portability limits
excludes: persistent login or host environment configuration
file-content parsing and transformation once command arguments have been formed

sample_tasks.instruction: In a POSIX shell, enumerate variables whose names start with BUILD_ and print each complete value, including empty values and embedded newlines, without exporting or changing the variables; explain any unavoidable portability limit.

A loop passes one stored filename as several command arguments and expands literal asterisks in another. Trace the expansions responsible and rewrite the argument construction so every original filename is preserved exactly.

sections.name: Transform files and records safely
sections.outcome: Select, rename, filter, join, sort, or aggregate files and records while preserving the relevant boundaries and preventing unintended matches, data loss, or overwrites.
includes: filename decomposition and reconstruction, null-delimited path handling, and collision checks
structured field selection, substitution, sorting, joining, counting, and malformed-record detection
excludes: explaining stream destinations, buffering, or event order in an operational incident
filesystem capacity, mount, and repair operations

sample_tasks.instruction: Given names such as ABC_1.fastq.Block12, including names with spaces, produce the corresponding _2 names while preserving every other component and refusing collisions or ambiguous matches.

From a large delimited dataset, report the ten most frequent status values only for valid rows, treating quoted delimiters correctly and rejecting malformed records instead of silently miscounting them.

sections.name: Control shell job execution
sections.outcome: Structure a repeated shell job so sequencing, exit status, retries, concurrency, temporary resources, interruption, and reruns have explicit and testable behavior.
includes: loops, conditionals, functions, pipelines as control flow, traps, temporary resources, and scheduled invocation
failure propagation, bounded concurrency, idempotence, dry runs, and partial-progress recording
excludes: the content-level correctness of a file or record transformation
persistent daemon supervision and service-manager configuration

sample_tasks.instruction: Write a batch driver that processes pending items at most four at a time, records each success, retries transient failures twice, cleans its private temporary directory on signals, and exits nonzero if any item remains failed.

A nightly script continues after a failed database export and deletes the previous good snapshot. Restructure its control flow so dependent steps require success, publication is atomic, and an interrupted rerun preserves the last verified snapshot.

sections.name: Provision a reproducible host runtime
sections.outcome: Prepare a host command or service to run predictably by selecting the packaged software and applying environment and time settings at the required scopes, then verify the combined behavior in new and existing processes.
includes: tasks coupling package state with process, user, or host runtime context
verification of executable provenance, inherited environment, locale-sensitive behavior, wall-clock display, and synchronization state
excludes: service topology, restart policy, and failure diagnosis after the runtime has been provisioned
building or releasing application source code

sample_tasks.instruction: Provision a reporting command from configured repositories, make it run in UTF-8 with a fixed timezone for one service account, and verify both the selected executable and the environment inherited by a newly started process without changing other users.

Preview an upgrade to a scheduled data tool, verify its dependency changes, configure the host clock and the job's locale for reproducible timestamps, and state which already running processes must be restarted to observe each change.

sections.name: Select and maintain packaged software
sections.outcome: Resolve a requested capability to the correct package and perform or reject an installation, removal, or upgrade based on exact metadata, repository state, dependency effects, and post-transaction verification.
includes: exact package metadata, file ownership lookup, configured repositories, dependencies, candidate versions, and holds or pins
transaction previews and verification of installed versions and executable provenance
excludes: language-specific dependency development from source
environment variables, locale, timezone, and service configuration

sample_tasks.instruction: A package search for git returns hundreds of descriptions. Identify the principal client and closely related official packages using exact package metadata, then verify which package owns the installed executable.

Before upgrading a shared command-line tool, report the candidate version and every package that the transaction would add, remove, or change, and retain the current version if the preview violates the stated constraint.

sections.name: Scope process environments and locales
sections.outcome: Configure environment variables, search paths, and locale behavior at invocation, process, user-session, or service scope and verify exactly which future processes inherit the change.
includes: environment inheritance, command-local assignments, login and non-login startup, service environments, PATH, and locale categories
distinguishing current shell state from persistent configuration for future processes
excludes: system clock synchronization and timezone databases
shell expansion bugs unrelated to configuring an execution environment

sample_tasks.instruction: Run one command with a different numeric locale, then configure the same locale for one user's future login sessions while leaving non-login batch jobs and other users unchanged; show how each scope is verified.

A service finds a different executable than an interactive shell. Trace the two inherited PATH values, set an explicit service environment, and verify the executable selected after starting a new service process.

sections.name: Configure system time and timezone
sections.outcome: Set and verify the host timezone, clock, and synchronization source while distinguishing absolute time from display conventions and accounting for already running processes.
includes: timezone selection, UTC offsets and daylight transitions, hardware and system clocks, synchronization status, and clock corrections
verification of host-wide changes and effects on timestamps, timers, and long-lived processes
excludes: locale categories other than timezone behavior
application scheduling policy unrelated to the host clock

sample_tasks.instruction: Change the system timezone for all users without rebooting, verify the active zone and synchronization state, and explain why stored UTC timestamps do not change while displayed civil times do.

A host clock is several minutes wrong even though its timezone label is correct. Determine whether synchronization is active and healthy, correct the clock safely, and verify the source and offset rather than merely changing the display zone.

sections.name: Diagnose and control service incidents
sections.outcome: Restore a failing or degraded service by correlating process lifecycle and resource evidence with stream or log evidence and service configuration, then apply a controlled change and verify recovery.
includes: incidents requiring evidence across process, logging, and service-manager boundaries
causal diagnosis, safe signal or configuration changes, health checks, and rollback criteria
excludes: application feature bugs with no operating-system cause
single-log queries or single-process controls that do not require cross-layer diagnosis

sample_tasks.instruction: A daemon repeatedly wakes before its intended deadline, grows in memory, and emits startup messages to both the terminal and a service log. Correlate signals, resource use, process instances, streams, and unit settings; then propose a controlled correction and recovery check.

A directory proxy starts successfully but intermittently returns incomplete results after reloads. Separate old and new process logs, check worker and descriptor pressure, validate backend and reload configuration, and define client checks plus a rollback trigger.

sections.name: Control processes and diagnose resource use
sections.outcome: Start, wait for, signal, and terminate related processes without races or orphans, and attribute abnormal CPU, memory, descriptor, or timing behavior to the responsible process or thread.
includes: process trees, jobs, exit status, signals, interrupted waits, deadlines, graceful termination, and escalation
per-process and per-thread CPU, memory, open-file, and descriptor observations
excludes: service-specific configuration syntax
reconstructing message destinations or order from standard streams and logs

sample_tasks.instruction: Explain why a thread's 60-second sleep repeatedly ends when another thread's timer signal is delivered, and revise the timing logic so it waits until the intended monotonic deadline.

A worker pool is slowing while host memory and open-file counts rise. Identify the responsible processes and resource class, distinguish a leak from expected cache or workload growth, and define a graceful shutdown sequence that leaves no workers behind.

sections.name: Trace process streams and logs
sections.outcome: Determine where operational messages went and reconstruct the defensible order and origin of events despite descriptor duplication, buffering, rotation, concurrent writers, and process restarts.
includes: standard input, output, and error; descriptor redirection and duplication; terminal and nohup behavior; buffering
log filtering, rotation, timestamps, process identity, boots, and restart boundaries
excludes: ordinary file or record transformation whose goal is a derived dataset
choosing pipeline data inputs and outputs when no operational diagnosis is requested

sample_tasks.instruction: A program prints some messages to the terminal and others to a redirected file, and their apparent order changes under nohup. Identify the descriptors and buffering involved and give capture options with explicit ordering guarantees and limits.

Investigate a service restart by selecting the relevant log window, separating rotated records and old versus new process instances, and identifying the earliest causal error rather than later shutdown symptoms.

sections.name: Configure and operate persistent services
sections.outcome: Translate a service topology into valid manager and daemon configuration, apply it with the least disruptive lifecycle action, and verify startup, dependencies, health, and client-visible behavior.
includes: configuration validation, dependency ordering, startup policy, reload versus restart, health checks, failover, and rollback
proxies and replicated backends when service topology determines request handling
excludes: host routing policy independent of a service topology
process resource diagnosis and stream-order reconstruction

sample_tasks.instruction: Configure a read-only proxy for two replicated directory backends serving the same naming context, validate the configuration before activation, and test complete results and failover from a client.

Roll out a daemon configuration change by checking syntax, selecting reload or restart from documented behavior, verifying dependencies and health, and using an explicit rollback point if client requests fail.

sections.name: Implement least-privilege host access
sections.outcome: Translate an access policy into accounts, group and file permissions, authentication controls, and narrowly delegated privileges, then test the combined allowed, denied, and audited paths from the affected identities.
includes: tasks requiring both resource permissions and an authentication or privileged-operation boundary
effective-identity testing, inheritance, negative tests, credential handling, and audit evidence
excludes: network route and name-resolution policy
application roles wholly internal to an application

sample_tasks.instruction: Provision a service account that can read one protected configuration tree and restart only its own daemon without an interactive privileged shell; verify inherited file access, rejected writes and unrelated commands, and audit records.

Onboard a project operator who authenticates with an individual credential, collaborates through a group-owned directory, and may run one fixed backup command; test new-file inheritance, outsider denial, privilege argument restrictions, and revocation.

sections.name: Administer identities and file permissions
sections.outcome: Create and retire users and groups and configure ownership, mode bits, ACLs, and inheritance so the effective file access of each relevant identity matches policy.
includes: account lifecycle, primary and supplementary groups, ownership, mode bits, ACLs, setgid directories, umask, and default permissions
effective identity and tests of allowed and denied filesystem operations
excludes: privileged command delegation and authentication-factor policy
packet filtering, routes, and remote service authorization

sample_tasks.instruction: Create a shared project directory where members of one group can create and edit files, new entries inherit the project group, and unrelated users cannot list or read contents; verify with representative identities.

Give one service account read-only traversal of a protected directory tree without changing access for other users, accounting for directory execute permission and existing ACL masks, then test one allowed and one denied path.

sections.name: Constrain authentication and privileged actions
sections.outcome: Configure authentication and privilege delegation so a named identity can perform only the intended administrative actions with attributable credentials and without escalation through arguments or environment.
includes: credential and key lifecycle, login restrictions, privilege delegation, fixed commands, environment sanitization, revocation, and auditability
testing interactive, non-interactive, allowed, denied, and escalation attempts
excludes: ordinary ownership, mode-bit, and ACL administration
application-specific authorization tokens and roles

sample_tasks.instruction: Allow an operator to execute one maintenance program as a service user without gaining a general privileged shell, passing arbitrary subcommands, or overriding its executable search path; demonstrate the accepted and rejected invocations.

Replace a shared administrative login with individual key-based identities, disable the obsolete credential, retain an emergency access path, and verify attribution and revocation without locking out current administrators.

sections.name: Establish and verify host connectivity
sections.outcome: Make a named remote endpoint reachable by coordinating route and source-address selection with name resolution and transport checks, and prove the chosen forward and return behavior under normal and failover conditions.
includes: tasks requiring both network-path policy and endpoint or resolver verification
multi-interface preference, failure behavior, DNS evidence, transport reachability, and client-context checks
excludes: service-layer backend selection after traffic reaches an application proxy
local users, file permissions, and privileged command policy

sample_tasks.instruction: Configure a multi-interface host so private names and destinations use the organization link, public traffic prefers cellular with Ethernet fallback, and trusted Wi-Fi supersedes both; verify resolver choice, selected source and route, and behavior as links change.

A named service resolves to reachable addresses but inbound sessions fail because replies leave through another gateway. Trace DNS answers, forward and return paths, source selection, and the transport test, then correct policy without breaking failover.

sections.name: Select and verify network paths
sections.outcome: Predict and configure the interface, gateway, and source address used for traffic based on prefixes, metrics, and policy rules, including return paths and link failures.
includes: longest-prefix matching, default routes, metrics, policy routing, interface state, source addresses, and asymmetric paths
route queries and packet-path observations under preference and failure changes
excludes: DNS record selection and application endpoint behavior
service-layer load balancing among backend instances

sample_tasks.instruction: Given three active interfaces and their subnets, propose routes and priorities that keep 10.0.0.0/8 on Ethernet, prefer cellular for other traffic, fall back to Ethernet, and override both when Wi-Fi connects.

A host accepts an inbound connection on one interface but sends replies through another gateway. Show the applicable route and policy decisions for both directions and correct the return-path selection.

sections.name: Diagnose names and transport endpoints
sections.outcome: Determine whether a connectivity failure arises in name resolution, address-family selection, listening endpoints, or transport reachability using observations from the affected client context.
includes: resolver configuration and search domains, DNS answers and caching, IPv4 and IPv6 selection, listening addresses and ports, and connection tests
distinguishing resolution, routing, filtering, refusal, and timeout evidence
excludes: changing route preference or policy rules
debugging application protocol correctness after a transport connection succeeds

sample_tasks.instruction: A service works by numeric IPv4 address but not by its short hostname for one user. Compare that user's resolver inputs and answers, search-domain expansion, cache state, and address-family choice to identify the failing layer.

A daemon reports healthy locally, but remote clients time out. Verify its listening address and port, test loopback and host-interface endpoints, and use the differing refusal or timeout evidence to locate the boundary without changing routes.

sections.name: Maintain recoverable storage
sections.outcome: Change or recover storage without losing service data by coordinating filesystem capacity and mount state with a verified backup or restore point, safe sequencing, and post-change integrity checks.
includes: operations whose safety depends on both live storage state and recoverability evidence
capacity remediation or migration with backup validation, quiescing, rollback, and service consistency checks
excludes: ordinary file transformation
remote replication treated as a backup without a recovery and retention contract

sample_tasks.instruction: A critical service is exhausting its filesystem. Identify the growth and mount constraints, verify a current restorable copy, move or extend the data safely, and confirm both service consistency and the ability to roll back.

Migrate application data to a new persistent volume while meeting a short recovery-point target: prepare and identify the filesystem, take a consistent backup, switch mounts, validate data and metadata, and rehearse reversal.

sections.name: Operate filesystems and capacity
sections.outcome: Inspect, mount, extend, and repair storage while accounting for device identity, filesystem state, byte and inode use, quotas, open files, and safe unmount requirements.
includes: block devices, partitions, filesystems, stable mount identity, persistent mounts, resizing, quotas, and repair preconditions
diagnosing deleted-but-open files, inode exhaustion, nested mounts, and space attribution
excludes: backup retention, recovery objectives, and restore validation
database-level consistency beyond identifying a need to quiesce it

sample_tasks.instruction: Disk usage remains full after a large log is deleted. Determine whether an open file, inode exhaustion, or a hidden nested mount explains the discrepancy and remediate without rebooting or deleting unrelated data.
Add a volume for application data, create and mount an appropriate filesystem persistently by stable identity, set ownership, and verify expected behavior after an unmount and mount cycle.

sections.name: Create and prove recoverable backups
sections.outcome: Choose and execute backup, snapshot, retention, and restore procedures that meet stated recovery goals, preserve required metadata and consistency, and demonstrate recovery through a tested restore.
includes: full and incremental copies, snapshots, application consistency, retention, encryption, integrity checks, and restore drills
recovery point and recovery time tradeoffs, staged restores, and selective recovery
excludes: high availability or replication alone
resizing, repairing, or mounting the live filesystem

sample_tasks.instruction: Plan backups for a changing dataset with a four-hour recovery-point target and limited repository capacity, including consistency, retention, encryption, integrity checks, and a timed restore drill.
Restore one accidentally deleted directory from an encrypted backup into staging, verify contents, ownership, ACLs, and timestamps, then return it to service without overwriting newer unrelated data.
